note: Recorded by hand from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/security_iam_nsd-with-iam-roles-service-linked.html. The candidate set is the 14 rows of the 'Supported Regions for AWS Shield network security director service-linked roles' table. Thirteen rows agree with themselves and are counted. One row does not: the page prints 'Africa (Cape Town) | ap-south-1', and Africa (Cape Town) is af-south-1 while ap-south-1 is Asia Pacific (Mumbai). Neither half of that row can be counted without asserting a Region the row itself contradicts, and the row text is not evidence for the Region the other column names, so it is recorded in unresolved and the numerator is 13. 13 covered + 0 excluded + 1 unresolved = 14 rows, so no row is silently dropped. All 13 counted codes are distinct, so there is no double count. Nothing is excluded: the page names no Region as unsupported, so derivation stays 'enumerated' and never 'universe-minus-exclusions'. Nothing is partial; the public-preview warning applies to the whole feature and is carried in notes. The IAM permissions policy earlier on the page contains action strings including 'ec2:DescribeRegions', 'cloudfront:ListDistributions' and 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancers'. Those are IAM actions, not Regions, services or resource types, and none of them is counted on any axis. No service-axis feature is emitted from the policy document, because a permission the role holds is not a statement of which services the feature analyses.
